newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ARSENAL VICTORY POINTS TO SERIOUS TITLE CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARSENAL VICTORY POINTS TO SERIOUS TITLE CHALLENGE.

text.p: The very fabric of what defines Arsenal Football Club was visibly demonstrated in 90 memorable minutes on Saturday when they scored a 2-1 win over Newcastle United to replace them at the top of the English premier league.

While Liverpool and Manchester United have dominated the English League down the decades, Arsenal are the only London side to have consistently matched their achievements and on Saturday's evidence it was not difficult to see why.
After only 22 minutes and with the scores level at 1-1, Arsenal had skipper Tony Adams sent off for a controversial "professional foul" on his England team mate Alan Shearer.
As Adams jogged off, Newcastle fans must have thought the three points were there for the taking.

But it was at that moment, that Arsenal 1996 turned into the Arsenal of Herbert Chapman's 1930s, the Arsenal that won the double in 1971, the Arsenal that won the FA Cup in 1979 with the last kick of the game, the Arsenal that consistently gets the better of arch-rivals Tottenham with last minute winners.
Their new manager Arsene -- can any manager be more aptly named? -- Wenger took off forward John Hartson and filled the gap in the defence left by Adams departure with stand-in Andy Linighan.

The Arsenal backline stood firm, Newcastle's ammunition was blunted against the red-shirted fortress built around John Lukic's goal, and Arsenal bided their time for the goal that eventually came, courtesy of Ian Wright after an hour.
As Wenger said afterwards: The sending-off changed the game for us after a good start. We had to defend for long spells after that, but I must congratulate my players at the way they came through it.
"I told the players that they would just have to keep going and that the chance would come to win the game if we kept Newcastle out -- it did."
Wenger added: "I am just glad that the chance fell to Ian Wright. Two men marking him is never enough and I'm never surprised when he scores _ ever.

The move contained its element of luck as Merson's mis-hit shot hit Ian Wright's foot but rolled into his path enabling him to control the ball and steer it left-footed past helpess Czech goalkeeper Pavel Srnicek.
And that, to all intents and purposes, was that. Newcastle huffed and puffed, but could not get back into the game.
Newcastle boss Keegan was scathing about his team's display as they slipped to their second defeat in succession and off the top of the table.
He warned: "It won't take many more performances like that before I start to change personnel. We were awful.
"It's never easy playing against 10 men, but the talent and inventiveness we had out there meant we should have created more.
"I never saw any of that inventiveness and it was a very disappointing all-round display from us.
So Arsenal left the field as league leaders, and only the most rabid of Tottenham fans could deny they are a very serious bet for the title.
The victory said everything about Arsenal's resilience, their never-say-die attitude and their organisation.

Wenger may only have been in charge for a few weeks, but he is clearly playing to Arsenal's traditional qualities of strength in defence and no-frills play in the build-up, although, it must be said, Arsenal's old "boring-boring" tag now looks out-of-date.
In many ways Arsenal's victory also starkly emphasised the historic differences between the two clubs who can both boast great past achievements.
But Newcastle's trophy cabinet has been bereft of serious silverware since 1969 when they won the old Inter Cities Fairs Cup. They haven't won the English title since 1927 or the F.A. Cup since 1955.
In contrast, Arsenal's 10 league titles, six F.A. Cup wins, their double and their four League Cup and European successes have all come since then.

Arsenal would never have let slip a 12-point lead in the way Newcastle did last season, and they probably would never have failed to beat a visiting side reduced to 10-men if the same circumstances that manisfested themselves at St James' Park on Saturday were re-enacted at Highbury.

There is still two-thirds of the English season to go, but if Arsenal do emerge as champions by just two points at the end of the season, there is absoutely no doubt about where those two points were won.
